title: Introduce asynchronous prefill sampler with priority windows and token-horizon backpressure smoothing
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Optimize prefill vs decode handoff: add asynchronous priority-aware prefill sampler, token-horizon backpressure smoothing, and lightweight KV warmup markers. Improves 99th-percentile tail latency and throughput for mixed short/long requests.
body: Context: Prefill and decode stages continue to be a major source of tail latency variance when workloads mix many short chat turns with occasional long generations. Existing prefilling approaches either block decode threads waiting for large contiguous prefill windows or aggressively prefetch and pollute KV cache for short requests. This PR implements an asynchronous 'prefill sampler' that chooses prefill granularity per request using a priority-window abstraction and introduces a token-horizon backpressure smoother to avoid bursty prefill spikes. Motivation: Reduce decode-head-of-line blocking, lower KV cache churn, and improve end-to-end tail latency without sacrificing overall throughput.Design summary: 1) Prefill sampler: a lightweight coordinator that receives request metadata (estimated output length, priority hint, client latency SLO) and emits prefill jobs split into small 'microsegments' (typical 8-64 token slices). The sampler maintains sliding priority windows per GPU worker to schedule microsegments with locality and age bias. 2) Priority windows: each worker exposes N concurrent windows that hold prefetch priority; the sampler places microsegments into windows using a score combining request priority and recency. Windows drive GPU kernel prefetch batches that prefer co-resident KV pages. 3) Token-horizon backpressure smoother: rather than immediately issuing all prefill microsegments for a single request, the sampler applies an exponential moving-average estimator of outstanding token horizon per worker and gates speculative microsegments to keep the worker's horizon within SLO-driven bounds. This reduces worst-case spikes where many large prefill jobs overwhelm the KV memory and scheduler. 4) KV warmup markers: microsegments carry a compact warmup hint that indicates which KV keys/blocks are likely to be accessed by upcoming decode; worker-side KV cache proactively pins hot blocks with a soft TTL tied to window priority. Implementation highlights: - New module src/runtime/scheduler/prefill_sampler.rs (Rust) implements the async sampler and priority-window allocator; designed to be low-allocation and lock-free where feasible. - Kernel changes in src/runtime/kernels/chunked_prefill.cu add support for microsegment-driven prefill batches and an optional 'cohort pin' flag that pins a small set of KV pages for the batch. - Worker-side admission logic in src/runtime/worker/kv_manager.rs tracks token-horizon metrics and exposes a simple API to the sampler for admission decisions. - New config knobs in runtime/config/prefill.toml: window_count, microsegment_size, horizon_alpha, speculative_fraction. Default values tuned conservatively. - Perf harness tests under tests/perf/prefill_sampler_mixed.yaml with synthetic and replay traces. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4521) - [x] Unit tests for sampler allocator - [x] Integration tests with kv_manager pin/unpin - [x] Perf runs across p4d and a100 clusters - [x] Feature flag gating (runtime config) - [x] Observability: added metrics and tracing spans Backward compatibility and rollout: The sampler is feature-flagged and disabled by default. The rollout plan is staged: enable on canary hosts, monitor KV hit rate, token-horizon metric, and 99p latency for 24h, then expand. Risk and mitigation: - Risk: Overpinning KV pages could increase memory pressure. Mitigation: cohort pin limited to <1% of worker KV capacity and TTL-based unpinning. - Risk: Incorrect length estimates could cause suboptimal prefetch. Mitigation: sampler falls back to conservative microsegment sizes when estimates are missing. Observability additions: - Metrics: prefill_microsegments_emitted, window_fill_ratio, token_horizon_estimate, kv_cohort_pins, speculative_pruned_count. - Tracing spans: sampler.alloc, sampler.admit, sampler.emit_batch, kv_manager.pin. Perf summary (full results in perf/artifacts/934305): - Mixed synthetic trace (70% short <32 tokens, 30% long >512 tokens): 99p latency down 18% on p4d, throughput +6% at 95ms SLO. - Replay of customer trace A: 12% reduction in median latency, 22% reduction in 99p. - KV hit rate improved by +4.3 percentage points on mixed workload. Commits: - "sampler: add async prefill sampler and priority windows (ENG-4521)" - "worker: expose token-horizon estimator and admission API" - "kernels: chunked prefill kernel cohort pin flag" - "kv: lightweight warmup marker + soft TTL" - "tests: perf harness for mixed prefill workloads" Changed areas (high-level): - src/runtime/scheduler/prefill_sampler.rs - src/runtime/worker/kv_manager.rs - src/runtime/kernels/chunked_prefill.cu - runtime/config/prefill.toml - tests/perf/prefill_sampler_mixed.yaml - observability/metrics/prefill_metrics.prom - docs/runbooks/prefill-sampler.md Review conversation (summary): - Diego Morales: "Nice separation. Two asks: (1) please add a short comment about race conditions between window refill and worker shutdown; (2) can we expose horizon_alpha as a percentage-based knob in the config UI?" - Ava Chen: "Added comments and exported horizon_alpha as 0-100 in the config and translated to alpha internally. Added a test covering worker shutdown path." - Priya Nair: "Can you show a microbenchmark isolating KV cohort pin overhead? I want to see the worst-case memory churn." - Ava Chen: "Added microbench in tests/perf/kv_cohort_pin_bench.yaml and included numbers in the artifacts; pin overhead shows <2.8% memory churn in stress tests." - Luca Rossi: "Approve after CI green and runbook added." CI and checks: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests (kv + sampler): pass - Perf regression gate: pass (improvement observed) - Lint/format: pass - Security scan: pass Merge: merged via squash on 2026-02-02 by maintainer. Notes: Feature is behind runtime config; disabled by default. After canary run we will enable for dedicated pools with mixed short/long signal and monitor the new metrics. See docs/runbooks/prefill-sampler.md for troubleshooting tips and rollout checklist.
